reagents.name: Sodium Borohydride
reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Hydride attacks prochiral ketones from both faces to give a racemic 2° alcohol unless a nearby chiral center biases face selectivity (Cram/Felkin-Anh).
reagents.rearrangementNote: Nucleophilic hydride transfer proceeds directly to the carbonyl carbon with zero carbocation formation.
reagents.conditions: MeOH or EtOH, 0–25 °C; mild aqueous workup
jeeTraps: Leaves esters, carboxylic acids, amides, nitriles, epoxides, nitro groups, and isolated C=C bonds completely untouched (unlike LiAlH4).
DOES reduce acid chlorides (RCOCl -> RCH2OH) and imines/iminium ions (reductive amination) even though esters do not react.
With α,β-unsaturated ketones, NaBH4 can give 1,2- and 1,4-reduction mixtures unless CeCl3 (Luche reagent) is added for selective 1,2-reduction to the allylic alcohol.

example.label: Chemoselective ketone reduction in presence of an ester

reagents.name: Lithium Aluminium Hydride

reactivity.epoxide: alcohol (SN2 attack at less hindered carbon)
reactivity.nitro: aliphatic R-NO2 -> 1° amine (R-NH2); aromatic Ar-NO2 -> azobenzene (Ar-N=N-Ar)
reactivity.alcohol: acid-base quench (evolves H2; recovers alcohol on H3O+ workup)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: SN2 backside hydride attack gives Walden inversion on epoxides (at the less substituted C) and 1°/2° alkyl halides; prochiral carbonyls give racemic alcohols.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Strong nucleophilic hydride transfer / SN2 displacement involves no carbocation intermediate.
reagents.conditions: Anhydrous Et2O or THF, 0 °C to reflux, then careful H3O+ workup
jeeTraps: Classic JEE Advanced trap: LiAlH4 reduces aliphatic R-NO2 to R-NH2, but reduces aromatic nitrobenzene (Ph-NO2) to AZOBENZENE (Ph-N=N-Ph), NOT aniline!
Reduces amides to amines (C=O -> CH2 without C–N cleavage), whereas esters cleave into two alcohols.
Leaves isolated C=C and C≡C untouched, EXCEPT conjugated cinnamaldehyde (Ph-CH=CH-CHO) which reduces fully to 3-phenylpropan-1-ol (Ph-CH2-CH2-CH2OH)!

example.label: Exhaustive reduction of both ketone and ester

reagents.name: Diisobutylaluminium Hydride (-78 °C)

reactivity.ester: aldehyde (1 equiv at -78 °C; stops at stable Al-hemiacetal)
reactivity.epoxide: alcohol (slow at -78 °C; electrophilic opening when warmed)
reactivity.alcohol: deprotonation (H2 evolved; recovers alcohol on workup)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Low-temperature ester/nitrile partial reduction stops cleanly at the tetrahedral Al-chelate; warming with internal alkynes gives syn-hydroalumination -> (Z)-alkene.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Lewis-acidic Al coordination followed by intramolecular hydride transfer causes no skeletal rearrangement.
reagents.conditions: 1 equiv in dry toluene or hexane at -78 °C, then cold H3O+ quench
jeeTraps: Strictly needs 1 equiv at -78 °C + cold aqueous workup to stop esters and nitriles at the aldehyde; at room temperature or with excess DIBAL-H, esters over-reduce to 1° alcohols.
Reduces BOTH esters and nitriles selectively to aldehydes without touching isolated alkenes, nitro groups, or alkyl halides.
Reduces α,β-unsaturated esters by 1,2-addition to α,β-unsaturated aldehydes (1 eq, -78 °C) or allylic alcohols (excess) while leaving the conjugated C=C intact.

example.label: Partial reduction of an ester to an aldehyde at -78 °C

reagents.name: Diborane in THF

reactivity.carboxylic_acid: 1° alcohol (FASTEST carbonyl reduction — beats esters, halides, nitro!)
reactivity.alcohol: slow H2 evolution (recovers alcohol on workup)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Lewis-acidic BH3 adds syn across π-bonds; chemoselective -COOH reduction preserves remote stereocenters.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Proceeds via concerted triacyloxyborane / hydroboration intermediates without carbocation rearrangement.
reagents.conditions: B2H6 or BH3·THF in anhydrous THF, 0–25 °C, then H3O+ workup
jeeTraps: Electrophilic reductant (opposite electronic preference to NaBH4/LiAlH4): reduces electron-rich -COOH FASTER than esters, acid chlorides, nitro groups, alkyl halides, and even ketones!
The textbook JEE reagent to reduce -COOH -> -CH2OH selectively in the presence of an ester (-COOR), -NO2, or -COCl.
Because BH3 also hydroborates C=C and C≡C bonds, alkenes are NOT spectators when using B2H6/THF!

example.label: Selective reduction of -COOH while leaving -COOMe untouched

reagents.name: Catalytic Hydrogenation (H2 / Pd-C)

reactivity.aldehyde: 1° alcohol (slow at 1 atm; faster with PtO2/Raney Ni)
reactivity.ketone: 2° alcohol (slow at 1 atm; faster with PtO2/Raney Ni)
reactivity.nitrile: 1° amine (with Raney Ni or high-pressure Pd-C)
reactivity.alkyne: alkane (complete reduction; does not stop at alkene)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Heterogeneous adsorption on the Pd surface delivers both H atoms to the same (less sterically hindered) face of C=C (strict syn-addition).
reagents.rearrangementNote: Surface-mediated radical/hydride transfer proceeds without carbocation rearrangement.
reagents.conditions: H2 (1 atm), 5–10% Pd/C in EtOH, MeOH, or EtOAc, 25 °C
jeeTraps: 1,2-Dimethylcyclohexene + H2/Pd-C yields exclusively cis-1,2-dimethylcyclohexane (meso, optically inactive) via syn-addition.
Selectively reduces C=C, C≡C, and Ar-NO2 at 1 atm while leaving benzene rings, esters, carboxylic acids, and amides untouched.
Also cleaves benzyl ethers (R-OBn -> R-OH + PhCH3) and benzyl esters by hydrogenolysis — a frequent JEE multi-step protection/deprotection trap.

example.label: Syn-hydrogenation of 1,2-dimethylcyclohexene to meso cis-isomer

reagents.name: Lindlar's Catalyst

reactivity.alkyne: cis-(Z)-alkene (syn-addition of 1 equiv H2; stops cleanly at alkene)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Poisoned Pd/CaCO3 surface delivers both H atoms syn across an internal alkyne to produce the cis/(Z)-alkene exclusively.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Heterogeneous surface syn-addition; zero rearrangement.
reagents.conditions: H2 (1 atm), Pd/CaCO3 poisoned with Pb(OAc)2 & quinoline, 25 °C
jeeTraps: Poisoning with Pb(OAc)2 and quinoline lowers surface activity so the alkene desorbs before further reduction to an alkane.
Always check whether the alkyne is internal or terminal: internal alkyne -> (Z)-alkene, whereas terminal alkyne -> 1-alkene (no cis/trans isomerism).
Classic multi-step JEE chain: internal alkyne + H2/Lindlar -> cis-alkene; then + Br2/CCl4 (anti) -> racemic dibromide (CAR), OR + OsO4 (syn) -> meso diol!

example.label: Syn semi-hydrogenation of an internal alkyne to (Z)-alkene

reagents.name: Dissolving Metal Reduction (Na / liq. NH3)

reactivity.ketone: 2° alcohol / pinacol (only if protic alcohol co-solvent added)
reactivity.carboxylic_acid: deprotonation (note: benzoic acid undergoes aromatic Birch ring reduction to 1,4-cyclohexadiene)
reactivity.alkyne: internal alkyne -> trans-(E)-alkene (anti-addition); terminal alkyne -> sodium acetylide (NO reduction!)
reactivity.alcohol: deprotonation (acts as proton source in Birch)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Single-electron transfer forms a trans-vinyl radical anion (minimizing steric/lone-pair repulsion), protonated sequentially to give the trans/(E)-alkene.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Stepwise radical-anion / vinyl-anion protonation involves zero carbocation rearrangement.
reagents.conditions: Na or Li metal in liquid NH3 at -33 °C (add EtOH for aromatic Birch)
jeeTraps: Terminal alkynes (R-C≡CH) are NOT reduced to alkenes by Na/liq. NH3 — the acidic terminal H is deprotonated immediately to R-C≡C⁻Na⁺ + 1/2 H2!
Stereochemical opposite of H2/Lindlar: internal alkyne -> (E)/trans-alkene, which then gives MESO dibromide with Br2/CCl4 (TAM) and RACEMIC diol with OsO4!
Aromatic Birch trap (Na/liq. NH3 + EtOH): electron-donating groups (-OMe, -Me) remain on the C=C of the 1,4-diene, whereas electron-withdrawing groups (-COOH) sit on the reduced sp3 carbon.

example.label: Anti semi-reduction of an internal alkyne to (E)-alkene

reagents.name: Clemmensen Reduction

reactivity.epoxide: ring opening (acid-sensitive — cleaved by conc. HCl)
reactivity.alcohol: substitution/dehydration (acid-sensitive: R-OH -> R-Cl or alkene in conc. HCl!)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Deoxygenates C=O completely to -CH2-; acid-sensitive chiral alcohols or epoxides elsewhere in the molecule are destroyed/racemized.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Deoxygenation itself does not rearrange, but co-existing acid-sensitive alcohols/alkenes/epoxides undergo carbocation dehydration or HCl addition in conc. HCl.
reagents.conditions: Zinc amalgam (Zn-Hg), conc. HCl, reflux
jeeTraps: NEVER use Clemmensen when acid-sensitive groups (-OH, acetal/ketal, epoxide, sensitive C=C) are present — conc. HCl converts -OH into -Cl or dehydrates it! Choose Wolff-Kishner instead.
Preferred over Wolff-Kishner when base-sensitive groups (alkyl halides, esters) are present because conc. HCl will not trigger E2 elimination.
Zn/conc. HCl simultaneously reduces aromatic -NO2 to -NH2 (as -NH3+Cl-) — a sneaky JEE multi-group trap!

example.label: Acidic deoxygenation of aryl ketone to alkylbenzene

reagents.name: Wolff-Kishner Reduction

reactivity.ester: saponification (hydrolyzed by hot KOH to carboxylate + alcohol)
reactivity.nitrile: slow hydrolysis to carboxylate in hot KOH
reactivity.alkyl_halide: alkene (base-sensitive: undergoes E2 elimination in hot KOH!)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Converts C=O to -CH2- via hydrazone deprotonation and N2 loss; strongly basic heat can epimerize enolizable α-stereocenters.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Anionic hydrazone decomposition avoids carbocation rearrangements completely.
reagents.conditions: NH2NH2·H2O, KOH, ethylene glycol (or diethylene glycol), 180–200 °C
jeeTraps: Go-to choice when acid-sensitive groups (-OH, acetal, isolated alkene) are present, because alcohols survive strongly basic KOH untouched (unlike Clemmensen!).
NEVER use Wolff-Kishner on substrates carrying base-sensitive alkyl halides (undergo E2 elimination!) or esters (saponify!) — use Clemmensen or neutral Mozingo (HSCH2CH2SH + Raney Ni).
If BOTH acid-sensitive (-OH) and base-sensitive (-Br) groups exist in one substrate, neither Clemmensen nor Wolff-Kishner is safe — use Mozingo thioacetal + Raney Ni!

example.label: Basic carbonyl deoxygenation preserving an acid-sensitive alcohol

reagents.name: Rosenmund Reduction

reactivity.acid_chloride: aldehyde (R-COCl -> R-CHO; stops cleanly at aldehyde)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Selective hydrogenolysis of the C–Cl bond in acyl chlorides to yield aldehydes cleanly.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Heterogeneous metal-catalyzed acyl-chloride reduction has no skeletal rearrangement.
reagents.conditions: H2, Pd supported on BaSO4 poisoned with S or quinoline in boiling xylene
jeeTraps: CANNOT prepare formaldehyde (HCHO) because formyl chloride (HCOCl) is unstable at room temperature!
CANNOT prepare ketones — Rosenmund reduces ONLY acid chlorides (RCOCl) to aldehydes (RCHO).
If BaSO4/S/quinoline poison is omitted, H2/Pd over-reduces the aldehyde straight to a 1° alcohol.

example.label: Partial reduction of an acyl chloride to an aldehyde

reagents.name: Stephen Reduction

reactivity.nitrile: aldehyde (via aldimine stannichloride R-CH=NH·HCl then H3O+)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Reduces linear -C≡N to an iminium salt, hydrolyzed to -CHO.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Two-electron reduction of nitrile followed by hydrolysis causes no rearrangement.
reagents.conditions: Anhydrous SnCl2, dry HCl gas in Et2O, then H3O+ / steam hydrolysis
jeeTraps: Reduces ONLY nitriles (R-C≡N -> R-CHO); unlike DIBAL-H, Stephen reagent does NOT reduce esters to aldehydes!
SnCl2/HCl ALSO reduces aromatic nitro groups (Ar-NO2 -> Ar-NH2) — watch for competing reduction in nitro-benzonitriles.
Ketones cannot be prepared by Stephen reduction (use R-CN + R'MgX then H3O+ to make ketones from nitriles).

example.label: Nitrile to aldehyde reduction via aldimine hydrolysis

reagents.name: Pyridinium Chlorochromate (PCC)

reactivity.alcohol: 1° alcohol -> aldehyde; 2° alcohol -> ketone; 3° alcohol -> no_reaction

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Mild anhydrous oxidation preserves double-bond (E)/(Z) geometry and remote stereocenters.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Standard 1°/2° alcohols oxidize with zero rearrangement; mildly acidic PCC can rearrange tertiary allylic alcohols (Babler oxidation).
reagents.conditions: C5H5NH+CrO3Cl- in strictly anhydrous CH2Cl2, 25 °C
jeeTraps: Stops 1° alcohols cleanly at the ALDEHYDE strictly because CH2Cl2 is anhydrous — water would hydrate RCHO to RCH(OH)2 and drive over-oxidation to RCOOH!
Oxidizes BOTH saturated aliphatic and allylic/benzylic 1° & 2° alcohols (unlike MnO2, which ignores saturated alcohols).
3° alcohols give NO reaction because they lack an α-C–H on the carbinol carbon.

example.label: Mild oxidation of 1° allylic alcohol to α,β-unsaturated aldehyde

reagents.name: Jones Reagent (CrO3 / aq. H2SO4)

reactivity.aldehyde: carboxylic acid (via gem-diol hydrate in aq. acid)
reactivity.alcohol: 1° alcohol -> carboxylic acid; 2° alcohol -> ketone; 3° alcohol -> no_reaction

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Oxidizes 1°/2° carbinol centers while leaving isolated C=C geometry and remote stereocenters intact at 0–25 °C.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Alcohol oxidation itself does not rearrange, though strongly acidic aq. H2SO4 can hydrolyze acetals or dehydrate acid-labile 3° alcohols.
reagents.conditions: CrO3, aq. H2SO4, acetone, 0–25 °C (orange Cr6+ -> green Cr3+)
jeeTraps: Water in aq. H2SO4 hydrates intermediate aldehydes to gem-diols RCH(OH)2, driving 1° alcohols all the way to CARBOXYLIC ACIDS (unlike anhydrous PCC!).
Unlike hot acidic KMnO4, cold Jones reagent in acetone leaves isolated C=C double bonds intact.
2° alcohols stop cleanly at ketones (ketones lack an α-C–H on the carbonyl carbon and resist chromic acid oxidation).

example.label: Strong oxidation of 1° alcohol to carboxylic acid leaving C=C intact

reagents.name: Cold Dilute Alkaline KMnO4 (Baeyer's Reagent)
reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Concerted [3+2] cycloaddition forms a cyclic manganate(V) ester delivering both -OH groups SYN (cis-2-butene -> meso diol; trans-2-butene -> racemic ± diol).
reagents.rearrangementNote: Concerted cyclic manganate ester formation involves zero carbocation rearrangement.
reagents.conditions: Cold (0–5 °C), dilute (1%) alkaline KMnO4 / H2O
jeeTraps: CIS + SYN = MESO (cis-2-butene -> meso-butane-2,3-diol, 1 optically inactive isomer); TRANS + SYN = RACEMIC (trans-2-butene -> (±)-pair)!
Baeyer's unsaturation test (purple -> brown MnO2 ppt) is positive for alkenes & alkynes, NEGATIVE for benzene rings.
Must stay cold and dilute — warming or acidifying cleaves the vicinal diol straight into ketones/carboxylic acids/CO2!

example.label: Syn-dihydroxylation: (Z)-but-2-ene -> meso-butane-2,3-diol

reagents.name: Hot Acidic KMnO4

reactivity.alkyne: oxidative cleavage: internal -> 2 RCOOH; terminal -> RCOOH + CO2
reactivity.alcohol: 1° alcohol -> carboxylic acid; 2° alcohol -> ketone; 3° alcohol -> no_reaction

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Complete C=C / C≡C cleavage destroys alkene stereochemistry.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Oxidative cleavage breaks the π and σ C–C bonds directly without carbocation shifts.
reagents.conditions: Conc. KMnO4, H2SO4 (or KOH then H3O+), heat / reflux
reagents.mechanismClass: Vigorous oxidative C=C / C≡C / benzylic cleavage
jeeTraps: Terminal =CH2 oxidizes all the way to CO2 + H2O (NOT formaldehyde or formic acid, because HCOOH oxidizes further to CO2!).
Benzylic oxidation trap: ANY alkylbenzene with ≥1 benzylic C–H (toluene, ethylbenzene, cumene) gives benzoic acid (Ph-COOH), while tert-butylbenzene (0 benzylic H!) gives NO reaction!
Produces carboxylic acids where reductive ozonolysis (O3/Zn) stops at aldehydes — cleavage products match O3/H2O2.

example.label: Oxidative C=C cleavage to carboxylic acid + ketone

reagents.name: Osmium Tetroxide Dihydroxylation
reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Concerted cyclic osmate ester guarantees 100% syn-dihydroxylation (cyclohexene -> cis-1,2-diol; cis-2-butene -> meso; trans-2-butene -> racemic).
reagents.rearrangementNote: Concerted [3+2] cycloaddition has zero carbocation character.
reagents.conditions: OsO4 (stoichiometric or catalytic + NMO), then aq. NaHSO3 / Na2SO3
jeeTraps: Exact same syn-stereochemistry as cold dil. KMnO4, but much milder and leaves aldehydes and alcohols untouched with zero C–C over-oxidation.
Opposite stereochemistry to mCPBA followed by H3O+ (which gives ANTI/trans-1,2-diol) and Br2/CCl4 (which is anti-addition)!
OsO4 + NaIO4 (Lemieux-Johnson) cleaves alkenes cleanly to aldehydes/ketones — exact same products as reductive ozonolysis (O3/Zn)!

example.label: Clean syn-dihydroxylation of cyclohexene to cis-1,2-diol

reagents.name: Reductive Ozonolysis (O3 then Zn/H2O)

reactivity.alkene: cleavage to aldehydes & ketones (=CH2 -> HCHO; =CHR -> RCHO; =CR2 -> R2C=O)
reactivity.alkyne: 1,2-diketone (mild Zn/H2O; partial cleavage to acids if prolonged)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Cleaves C=C completely via molozonide -> ozonide; Zn/H2O or Me2S quenches H2O2 so aldehydes do NOT over-oxidize.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Concerted Criegee 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition/cycloreversion does not rearrange carbon skeletons.
reagents.conditions: 1) O3, CH2Cl2 at -78 °C; 2) Zn/H2O (or Me2S / PPh3)
jeeTraps: Zn/H2O or Me2S destroys H2O2 so aldehydes survive intact — even terminal =CH2 stops at formaldehyde (HCHO), NOT CO2!
JEE counting classic: reductive ozonolysis of o-xylene gives glyoxal : methylglyoxal : diacetyl in a 3 : 2 : 1 molar ratio (proving Kekulé resonance equivalence).
Switching workup to NaBH4 reduces the ozonide directly to alcohols (1° from =CHR, 2° from =CR2)!

example.label: Reductive cleavage stopping cleanly at aldehyde + ketone

reagents.name: Oxidative Ozonolysis (O3 then H2O2)

reactivity.alkene: cleavage to carboxylic acids & ketones (=CH2 -> CO2; =CHR -> RCOOH; =CR2 -> R2C=O)
reactivity.alkyne: cleavage to carboxylic acids (internal -> 2 RCOOH; terminal -> RCOOH + CO2)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Oxidative workup breaks the ozonide and oxidizes every C–H carbonyl fragment all the way to -COOH / CO2.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Criegee ozonolysis with oxidative workup involves zero carbocation rearrangement.
reagents.conditions: 1) O3, CH2Cl2 at -78 °C; 2) H2O2 / H2O (or plain H2O without Zn!)
jeeTraps: Huge JEE trap: O3 followed by plain H2O (WITHOUT Zn or Me2S!) generates H2O2 in situ, so it IS oxidative ozonolysis and turns aldehydes into carboxylic acids!
Terminal =CH2 oxidizes via HCOOH to CO2 + H2O, while =CHR yields RCOOH and =CR2 stops at a ketone.
Internal alkynes cleave cleanly into two carboxylic acids (R-COOH + R'-COOH), matching hot acidic KMnO4.

example.label: Oxidative cleavage converting =CHR fragment to carboxylic acid

reagents.name: Activated Manganese Dioxide

reactivity.alcohol: allylic / benzylic / propargylic 1° -> aldehyde, 2° -> ketone; saturated aliphatic alcohols -> NO REACTION!

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Mild neutral surface oxidation preserves double-bond (E)/(Z) stereochemistry and remote chiral centers.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Resonance-stabilized allylic/benzylic radical surface step causes no skeletal rearrangement.
reagents.conditions: Activated MnO2 (excess) in CH2Cl2, CHCl3, or hexane, 25 °C
jeeTraps: Oxidizes ONLY allylic, benzylic, and propargylic 1°/2° alcohols — completely ignores saturated aliphatic 1° and 2° alcohols in the same molecule (unlike PCC/Jones)!
Stops allylic/benzylic 1° alcohols cleanly at the aldehyde without over-oxidation to -COOH and without cis/trans isomerization.
3° allylic/benzylic alcohols do NOT react (no α-H on carbinol carbon).

example.label: Chemoselective oxidation of benzylic -OH over saturated 1° -OH

reagents.name: Periodic Acid (Malaprade Cleavage)

reactivity.alcohol: vicinal 1,2-diols, α-hydroxy carbonyls, 1,2-diketones & 1,2-amino alcohols -> C–C cleavage; isolated alcohols & 1,3-diols -> no_reaction

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Requires formation of a 5-membered cyclic periodate ester: cis-1,2-diols cleave rapidly while rigid trans-diaxial cyclic 1,2-diols fail to react.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Concerted cyclic periodate ester cleavage breaks the C–C bond directly.
reagents.conditions: HIO4 or NaIO4 in H2O / aq. MeOH, 25 °C
jeeTraps: Each cleaved C–C bond consumes 1 equiv HIO4 and adds +1 OH equivalent to each end: terminal -CH2OH -> HCHO; internal -CH(OH)- (cleaved twice) -> HCOOH; -CH(OH)R -> RCHO; -C(OH)R2 -> R2C=O; -CHO -> HCOOH; -COR -> RCOOH!
Classic JEE stoichiometry: glycerol consumes 2 HIO4 (-> 2 HCHO + 1 HCOOH); open-chain D-glucose consumes 5 HIO4 (-> 5 HCOOH + 1 HCHO).
Simple mono-alcohols, 1,3-diols, and rigid trans-diaxial cyclic 1,2-diols cannot form the cyclic periodate ester and do NOT cleave!

example.label: Malaprade cleavage of glycerol (2 equiv HIO4)

reagents.name: Tollens' Reagent (Ammoniacal AgNO3)

reactivity.aldehyde: carboxylate salt + Ag(s) silver mirror (BOTH aliphatic AND aromatic aldehydes!)
reactivity.alkyne: terminal alkyne -> white ppt of silver acetylide (R-C≡C-Ag, acid-base, not redox!)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Mild oxidation of -CHO to -COO- leaves double bonds and remote stereocenters intact.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Mild single-electron Ag(I) oxidation involves no skeletal rearrangement.
reagents.conditions: Freshly prepared [Ag(NH3)2]+OH- (aq. AgNO3 + NH4OH), warm gently
jeeTraps: Positive for BOTH aliphatic AND aromatic aldehydes (e.g. benzaldehyde), distinguishing it from Fehling's which fails on aromatic aldehydes!

JEE classic positive exceptions (not ordinary aldehydes): formic acid (HCOOH -> CO2 + Ag), α-hydroxy ketones (fructose & benzoin via enediol), reducing sugars/hemiacetals (glucose, maltose, lactose), and PhNHOH! Sucrose (acetal) is NEGATIVE.
Terminal alkynes react with ammoniacal AgNO3 to form a WHITE precipitate (R-C≡C-Ag), NOT a silver mirror!

example.label: Silver mirror oxidation of an aromatic aldehyde

reagents.name: Fehling's Solution (Alkaline Cu2+ Tartrate)

reactivity.aldehyde: aliphatic aldehyde -> carboxylate + brick-red Cu2O ppt; AROMATIC aldehyde -> NO REACTION!

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Weak alkaline Cu(II) oxidant selectively converts aliphatic -CHO to -COO-.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Direct oxidation of aliphatic aldehyde; note sugars undergo alkaline enediol tautomerism.
reagents.conditions: Fehling A (aq. CuSO4) + Fehling B (alkaline Na/K tartrate, Rochelle salt), heat
jeeTraps: THE canonical JEE test separating aliphatic aldehydes (POSITIVE -> red-brown Cu2O ppt) from aromatic aldehydes like benzaldehyde (NEGATIVE, resonance-stabilized -CHO)!
Fructose (ketose) gives a POSITIVE Fehling's test via alkaline enediol isomerization to glucose/mannose, while sucrose (locked glycosidic acetal) is NEGATIVE.
Benzoin (Ph-CH(OH)-CO-Ph) gives POSITIVE Tollens' test but NEGATIVE Fehling's test — a favorite JEE Advanced discrimination question!

example.label: Brick-red Cu2O oxidation of an aliphatic aldehyde

reagents.name: meta-Chloroperoxybenzoic Acid (mCPBA)

reactivity.ketone: ester / cyclic ketone -> lactone (Baeyer-Villiger; migratory aptitude: H > 3° > 2° ≈ Ph > 1° > Me)
reactivity.alkene: epoxide (concerted syn-epoxidation; faster on MORE substituted electron-rich C=C!)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Concerted butterfly TS gives 100% stereospecific syn-epoxidation (cis-alkene -> cis-epoxide, trans -> trans); Baeyer-Villiger proceeds with 100% RETENTION at the migrating chiral carbon.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Epoxidation has zero rearrangement; Baeyer-Villiger is a concerted stereoretentive 1,2-shift to electron-deficient O.
reagents.conditions: mCPBA in CH2Cl2 or CHCl3, 0–25 °C
jeeTraps: Electrophilic reagent: in a non-conjugated diene, mCPBA selectively epoxidizes the MORE substituted (more electron-rich) C=C double bond!
mCPBA followed by H3O+ (or OH-/H2O) achieves overall ANTI-dihydroxylation (trans-1,2-diol), directly opposite to OsO4/cold KMnO4 syn-dihydroxylation!
Baeyer-Villiger O-insertion follows electron-rich migratory aptitude (H > 3° > cyclohexyl > 2° ≈ Ph > 1° > Me) with strict RETENTION of configuration at a chiral migrating group.

example.label: Stereospecific syn-epoxidation of (Z)-but-2-ene

reagents.name: Selenium Dioxide (Riley Oxidation)

reactivity.aldehyde: α-dicarbonyl / glyoxal (oxidizes active α-CH2/CH3 next to -CHO to C=O)
reactivity.ketone: 1,2-diketone (oxidizes active α-CH2/CH3 next to C=O to C=O)
reactivity.alkene: allylic alcohol (oxidizes allylic C–H without cleaving C=C; CH2 > CH3 > CH)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Allylic oxidation via ene + [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement selectively oxidizes the (E)-methyl on trisubstituted alkenes to give the (E)-allylic alcohol.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Concerted ene + [2,3]-sigmatropic shift restores the original double-bond position with no carbocation shift.
reagents.conditions: SeO2 in EtOH/H2O, AcOH, or 1,4-dioxane, reflux
jeeTraps: Oxidizes the α-CH2 (or α-CH3) adjacent to an aldehyde or ketone directly into C=O (acetaldehyde -> glyoxal; acetone -> methylglyoxal; cyclohexanone -> cyclohexane-1,2-dione).
On unsymmetrical ketones, oxidizes the LESS sterically hindered α-CH2 preferentially over -CH3 (CH2 > CH3 > CH).
Does NOT cleave C=C bonds (unlike O3 or hot KMnO4) — converts alkenes cleanly to allylic alcohols!

example.label: Riley α-oxidation of cyclohexanone to 1,2-diketone

reagents.name: Hydrobromic Acid (Ionic / Dark)

reactivity.alkene: Markovnikov alkyl bromide (via carbocation — HIGH rearrangement risk!)
reactivity.alkyne: Markovnikov vinyl bromide (1 eq) -> gem-dibromide (2 eq)
reactivity.epoxide: bromohydrin (acid-catalyzed attack at MORE substituted carbon)
reactivity.alcohol: alkyl bromide (1° SN2; 2°/3° SN1 with rearrangement)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Planar sp2 carbocation intermediate suffers nucleophilic Br- attack from both faces -> non-stereospecific syn + anti (racemic) mixture.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Free carbocation intermediate readily undergoes 1,2-hydride shift, 1,2-methyl shift, or ring expansion before Br- traps it!
reagents.conditions: HBr in CCl4, AcOH, or dark/peroxide-free conditions
jeeTraps: 3-Methylbut-1-ene + HBr gives 2-bromo-2-methylbutane (via 2° -> 3° 1,2-hydride shift) as MAJOR product, NOT 2-bromo-3-methylbutane!
Watch for ring expansion on vinylcyclobutane / vinylcyclopentane derivatives whenever a 2° carbocation sits adjacent to a strained 4- or 5-membered ring.
Acid-catalyzed epoxide opening with HBr puts Br at the MORE substituted carbon (SN1-like TS), opposite to basic Nu-/RMgX opening!

example.label: Markovnikov addition WITH 1,2-hydride shift carbocation rearrangement

reagents.name: HBr with Peroxide (Kharasch Effect)

reactivity.alkene: anti-Markovnikov alkyl bromide (via radical chain; ZERO rearrangement!)
reactivity.alkyne: anti-Markovnikov vinyl bromide (1 eq) -> vicinal 1,2-dibromide (2 eq)
reactivity.epoxide: bromohydrin (acid-catalyzed attack at MORE substituted carbon)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Planar carbon free-radical intermediate gives non-stereospecific syn + anti (racemic) addition.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Free radicals do NOT undergo 1,2-hydride or 1,2-methyl shifts — carbon skeleton remains 100% intact!
reagents.conditions: HBr + organic peroxide (ROOR / BPO) or hν
jeeTraps: WORKS ONLY FOR HBr! HCl/ROOR (H-abstraction endothermic) and HI/ROOR (I• addition endothermic) BOTH still give ionic MARKOVNIKOV products!
ZERO carbocation rearrangement because the intermediate is a carbon radical (3-methylbut-1-ene -> 1-bromo-3-methylbutane cleanly).
Br• adds FIRST to the LESS substituted alkene carbon specifically to form the MORE stable carbon radical (3° > 2° > 1°).

example.label: Anti-Markovnikov radical addition with ZERO rearrangement

reagents.name: Acid-Catalyzed Hydration (dil. H2SO4 / H2O)

reactivity.ester: carboxylic acid + alcohol (reversible hydrolysis on heating)
reactivity.alkene: Markovnikov alcohol via carbocation (HIGH rearrangement risk!)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Planar carbocation gives non-stereospecific racemic alcohol on alkenes; protonated epoxides open with anti-stereochemistry.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Free carbocation intermediate readily undergoes 1,2-hydride shift, 1,2-methyl shift, and ring expansion (e.g. 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene -> 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol).
reagents.conditions: Dilute aq. H2SO4 (or H3PO4), moderate heat
jeeTraps: 3,3-Dimethylbut-1-ene + H3O+ rearranges via 1,2-methyl shift to 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol (3° alcohol) — unlike oxymercuration which gives unrearranged 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol!
Alkynes require HgSO4/H2SO4 (Kucherov hydration): ethyne is the ONLY alkyne giving an aldehyde (CH3CHO); all higher alkynes give ketones.
Equilibrium trap: dilute H2SO4 hydrates alkenes to alcohols, while conc. H2SO4 + heat dehydrates alcohols to Zaitsev alkenes!

example.label: Carbocation hydration WITH 1,2-methyl shift rearrangement

reagents.name: Oxymercuration-Demercuration
reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Step 1 (oxymercuration via bridged mercurinium ion) is anti-addition, but Step 2 (NaBH4 radical demercuration) scrambles C–Hg stereochemistry -> overall non-stereospecific (syn + anti) mixture.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Bridged cyclic mercurinium ion prevents free carbocation formation — ZERO 1,2-hydride/methyl shifts or ring expansions!
reagents.conditions: 1) Hg(OAc)2, THF/H2O; 2) NaBH4, aq. NaOH
jeeTraps: Delivers the UNREARRANGED Markovnikov alcohol (3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene -> 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol), contrasting sharply with H3O+!
Replacing H2O with an alcohol solvent (MeOH/EtOH) performs alkoxymercuration-demercuration to give the unrearranged Markovnikov ETHER!
Overall addition is NOT purely anti because NaBH4 demercuration goes via a free radical; using NaBD4 places D at the LESS substituted carbon (and NaBH4 will reduce any ketone/aldehyde also present!).

example.label: Unrearranged Markovnikov hydration via cyclic mercurinium ion

reagents.name: Hydroboration-Oxidation

reactivity.alkene: anti-Markovnikov alcohol via strict SYN-addition with ZERO rearrangement!
reactivity.alkyne: terminal alkyne -> aldehyde; internal alkyne -> ketone (via anti-Markovnikov enol)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Concerted 4-center syn-hydroboration + H2O2/OH- oxidation with 100% RETENTION at the C–B bond installs H and OH strictly SYN (e.g. 1-methylcyclohexene -> trans-2-methylcyclohexanol!).
reagents.rearrangementNote: Concerted 4-membered transition state produces zero carbocation and zero skeletal rearrangement.
reagents.conditions: 1) BH3·THF (or 9-BBN / Sia2BH); 2) H2O2, aq. NaOH
jeeTraps: 1-Methylcyclohexene + BH3·THF then H2O2/OH- yields TRANS-2-methylcyclohexanol (±) because H and OH add SYN, placing -CH3 and -OH trans to each other!
Terminal alkynes + hydroboration-oxidation (especially bulky Sia2BH / 9-BBN) give ALDEHYDES (opposite of HgSO4/H2SO4 which gives methyl ketones!).
Deuterium trap: BD3·THF then H2O2/OH- puts D on the MORE substituted carbon and -OH on the LESS substituted carbon (syn); BH3 then CH3COOD puts D on the LESS substituted carbon (alkane)!

example.label: Anti-Markovnikov syn-hydration with zero rearrangement

reagents.name: Bromine in Carbon Tetrachloride

reactivity.alkene: trans/anti-vicinal dibromide (red-brown Br2 decolorizes; via cyclic bromonium ion)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Cyclic bromonium ion forces strict backside ANTI-addition of Br- (CAR/TAM: cis-2-butene -> racemic ± pair; trans-2-butene -> meso-2,3-dibromobutane).
reagents.rearrangementNote: Bridged 3-membered bromonium ion prevents carbocation rearrangement (rare exceptions only for strongly aryl-stabilized styrenes).
reagents.conditions: Br2 in inert anhydrous CCl4 or CH2Cl2, dark, 0–25 °C
jeeTraps: CAR / TAM rule (opposite of OsO4/cold KMnO4): trans-2-butene + Br2/CCl4 (anti) -> MESO-2,3-dibromobutane, while cis-2-butene -> RACEMIC (±) pair!
Switching solvent to water (Br2/H2O) traps the bromonium ion with H2O at the MORE substituted carbon -> anti-bromohydrin (Br on less substituted C, OH on more substituted C).
Decolorizes reddish-brown Br2 for alkenes/alkynes, NOT benzene (needs FeBr3 Lewis acid).

example.label: Anti-addition (TAM): (E)-but-2-ene -> meso-2,3-dibromobutane

reagents.name: SN1 Unimolecular Nucleophilic Substitution

reactivity.epoxide: acid-catalyzed ring opening at MORE substituted carbon
reactivity.alkyl_halide: 3° / benzylic / allylic R-X -> substitution (rate = k[RX]; competes with E1)
reactivity.alcohol: 3° / benzylic / allylic R-OH + HX -> R-X (via carbocation with rearrangement!)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Planar sp2 carbocation produces racemization with slight excess of inversion (~55:45) due to intimate ion-pair shielding by departing X-.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Free carbocation intermediate undergoes fast 1,2-hydride/methyl shifts and ring expansion (e.g. neopentyl bromide + AgNO3/EtOH rearranges completely to tert-amyl ether!).
reagents.conditions: Polar protic solvent (H2O, EtOH, AcOH), weak nucleophile / heat (or AgNO3 catalyst)
jeeTraps: Rate is independent of [Nu]; substrate reactivity: benzyl/allyl ≈ 3° > 2° >> 1° > CH3, and bridgehead halides (1-bromonorbornane) are COMPLETELY UNREACTIVE (Bredt's rule — cannot flatten!).
JEE Advanced stereo nuance: SN1 gives racemization with SLIGHT EXCESS OF INVERSION (not exact 50:50) because the leaving anion shields the front face in the tight ion pair.
AgNO3/EtOH pulls off X- as insoluble AgX, forcing SN1 carbocation rearrangement even on 1° neopentyl bromide!

example.label: Solvolysis of chiral 3° bromide with racemization

reagents.name: SN2 Bimolecular Nucleophilic Substitution

reactivity.epoxide: ring opening at LESS hindered carbon with inversion
reactivity.alkyl_halide: CH3 > 1° > 2° R-X -> substituted product (3° R-X: NO SN2 -> E2!); rate = k[RX][Nu]

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Concerted 180° backside attack through a pentacoordinate transition state yields 100% Walden inversion.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Single concerted step — zero carbocation formation and zero skeletal rearrangement.
reagents.conditions: Polar aprotic solvent (DMSO, DMF, acetone, MeCN), strong unhindered nucleophile (CN-, I-, RS-, N3-)
jeeTraps: Solvent nucleophilicity flip: in polar APROTIC solvents (DMSO/DMF) halide reactivity is F- > Cl- > Br- > I-, whereas in polar PROTIC solvents (H2O/EtOH) it reverses to I- > Br- > Cl- > F-!
Neopentyl bromide ((CH3)3C-CH2Br) is a 1° halide yet is ~100,000× slower in SN2 than ethyl bromide due to massive β-branching steric hindrance.
Walden inversion always flips 3D configuration, BUT the CIP (R)/(S) label can stay the same if the incoming nucleophile alters priority numbering — always recompute CIP!

example.label: Backside SN2 displacement with 100% Walden inversion (R -> S)

reagents.name: Zaitsev E2 Elimination (Small Strong Base)

reactivity.epoxide: ring opening at less hindered carbon
reactivity.alkyl_halide: more substituted (Zaitsev) trans-alkene (2°/3° R-X; 1° R-X prefers SN2 ether)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Strict anti-periplanar (180° dihedral) elimination of β-H and leaving group; cyclohexyl halides MUST adopt a diaxial (trans-diaxial) chair conformation.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Concerted one-step β-elimination — zero carbocation rearrangement.
reagents.conditions: NaOEt/EtOH or alc. KOH (small unhindered strong base), heat
jeeTraps: Anti-periplanar ring trap: trans-1-bromo-2-methylcyclohexane cannot place Br and C2-H trans-diaxial simultaneously, so it eliminates exclusively toward C6 -> 3-methylcyclohexene (Hofmann-like!) even with EtO-!
Poor leaving groups (-F, -NR3+, -SR2+) give the HOFMANN (less substituted) alkene even with small EtO- because the transition state becomes carbanion-like (E1cb-like)!
Shows a large primary kinetic isotope effect (k_H / k_D ≈ 3–7) since C–H cleavage is rate-determining.

example.label: Zaitsev elimination to the more substituted internal alkene

reagents.name: Hofmann E2 Elimination (Bulky Strong Base)

reactivity.epoxide: slow opening at least hindered carbon
reactivity.alkyl_halide: less substituted (Hofmann) alkene (1°/2°/3° R-X; suppresses SN2 even on 1° halides!)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Concerted anti-periplanar β-elimination dominated by steric accessibility of the least hindered β-hydrogen.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Single concerted E2 step — zero carbocation rearrangement.
reagents.conditions: t-BuOK in t-BuOH (or bulky DBU / Et3N), heat
reagents.mechanismClass: Sterically controlled anti-periplanar Hofmann E2 elimination
jeeTraps: Steric bulk of t-BuO- selects the most accessible 1° β-H, flipping regioselectivity from Zaitsev (2-methylbut-2-ene) to Hofmann (2-methylbut-1-ene)!
Forces E2 elimination even on 1° alkyl halides (e.g. 1-bromobutane -> 1-butene) where small EtO- would instead perform Williamson SN2!
Conjugation exception: if elimination produces a conjugated styrene/diene, resonance stabilization can still override bulky-base Hofmann preference.

example.label: Hofmann elimination to the less substituted terminal alkene

reagents.name: Thionyl Chloride with Pyridine (Darzens SN2)

reactivity.alcohol: alkyl chloride with COMPLETE INVERSION of configuration (SN2 via free Cl-)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Pyridine scavenges HCl to liberate nucleophilic Cl-, which displaces the chlorosulfite (-OSOCl) via backside SN2 -> 100% INVERSION.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Concerted SN2 displacement on the alkyl chlorosulfite avoids carbocation rearrangements.
reagents.conditions: SOCl2, pyridine (1 equiv), dry ether/CH2Cl2, 0–25 °C
reagents.mechanismClass: SN2 backside displacement on alkyl chlorosulfite
jeeTraps: THE #1 JEE chlorination stereochemistry trap: adding Pyridine switches SOCl2 from SNi (RETENTION) to SN2 (INVERSION) because pyridine generates free external Cl-!
Converts 1° and 2° alcohols cleanly into R-Cl WITHOUT carbocation rearrangement (unlike HCl/ZnCl2 Lucas reagent).
Also converts carboxylic acids cleanly into acid chlorides (RCOCl) and dehydrates 1° amides to nitriles.

example.label: Chlorination of chiral 2° alcohol with complete INVERSION (S -> R)

reagents.name: Thionyl Chloride Neat (SNi Retention)

reactivity.alcohol: alkyl chloride with RETENTION of configuration (SNi internal front-side delivery)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Internal nucleophilic substitution (SNi): the alkyl chlorosulfite (R-O-SOCl) collapses via a tight intimate ion pair delivering Cl- from the SAME face -> RETENTION.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Tight intimate ion-pair collapse suppresses free carbocation shifts on standard 2° alcohols.
reagents.conditions: Neat SOCl2 (or in Et2O / 1,4-dioxane), gentle warming; SO2↑ + HCl↑ escape as gases
reagents.mechanismClass: Internal nucleophilic substitution (SNi) via intimate ion pair
jeeTraps: Neat SOCl2 (no pyridine!) gives RETENTION via SNi, directly opposite to SOCl2/Pyridine which gives INVERSION via SN2!
Solvent trap: in 1,4-dioxane, solvent neighboring-group participation causes double inversion -> still overall RETENTION!
PCl5, PCl3, and PBr3 with chiral 2° alcohols ALWAYS give INVERSION (SN2), never SNi retention.

example.label: SNi chlorination of chiral 2° alcohol with RETENTION (S -> S)

reagents.name: Grignard Reagent (RMgX)

reactivity.ketone: 3° alcohol (1,2-addition even on unhindered α,β-unsaturated ketones)
reactivity.ester: 3° alcohol (adds 2 equiv RMgX via ketone; formate ester -> 2° alcohol)
reactivity.carboxylic_acid: acid-base quench ONLY (forms R-H alkane + R'COOMgX; consumes RMgX!)
reactivity.acid_chloride: 3° alcohol (adds 2 equiv RMgX — does NOT stop at ketone!)
reactivity.amide: acid-base quench (1°/2° amide) or sluggish (3° amide; Weinreb amide stops at ketone)
reactivity.nitrile: ketone (adds 1 equiv -> imine salt -> H3O+ gives R'-CO-R)
reactivity.alkyne: terminal alkyne -> acid-base quench (R-H + R'-C≡C-MgX); internal -> no_reaction
reactivity.epoxide: alcohol (+2 C with ethylene oxide; SN2 attack at LESS hindered carbon)
reactivity.alcohol: acid-base quench ONLY (forms R-H alkane + R'OMgX — Zerewitinoff active-H trap!)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: SN2 backside ring opening of epoxides gives inversion at the less hindered carbon; carbonyl additions give racemic alcohols unless Cram/Felkin-Anh biased.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Carbanion-like nucleophilic addition / SN2 involves zero carbocation rearrangement.
reagents.conditions: Anhydrous Et2O or THF, 0–25 °C (strictly moisture/O2-free), then H3O+ workup
jeeTraps: Zerewitinoff active-H trap: ANY protic H (-OH, -COOH, -NH, -SH, terminal -C≡CH, H2O) instantaneously protonates RMgX to alkane R-H before carbonyl attack!
Esters and acid chlorides consume 2 equiv RMgX to yield 3° alcohols — cannot stop at a ketone (use Gilman R2CuLi or R2Cd for RCOCl -> ketone!).
On α,β-unsaturated ketones, hard RMgX prefers direct 1,2-addition to C=O, whereas soft Gilman R2CuLi gives 1,4-conjugate (Michael) addition.

example.label: Double addition of MeMgBr to benzoyl chloride -> 3° alcohol

reagents.name: Gilman Reagent (Lithium Dialkylcuprate)

reactivity.aldehyde: 2° alcohol (sluggish at -78 °C; much less reactive than RMgX)
reactivity.ketone: no_reaction (saturated ketones untouched; α,β-unsaturated ketones -> 1,4-Michael addition!)
reactivity.acid_chloride: ketone (STOPS CLEANLY at ketone without 2nd addition!)
reactivity.epoxide: alcohol (SN2 opening at LESS hindered carbon)
reactivity.alkyl_halide: alkane (Corey-House coupling with 1°/2° alkyl, vinyl, and aryl halides!)

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Corey-House coupling on chiral 2° halides/tosylates proceeds with inversion; vinyl halides couple with RETENTION of E/Z geometry; epoxides open with SN2 inversion.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Oxidative-addition / reductive-elimination organocopper pathway avoids carbocation rearrangement.
reagents.conditions: R2CuLi (from 2 RLi + CuI) in dry Et2O or THF, -78 °C to 0 °C, then H3O+
reagents.mechanismClass: Soft organocopper acyl substitution / 1,4-conjugate / Corey-House coupling
jeeTraps: Converts acid chlorides (RCOCl) cleanly into KETONES and stops there because soft R2CuLi does NOT react with saturated ketones or esters!
On α,β-unsaturated ketones (enones), R2CuLi delivers exclusive 1,4-conjugate (Michael) addition — the exact regioselective complement to Grignard 1,2-addition!
Corey-House synthesis couples R2CuLi with 1° alkyl, vinyl (with E/Z retention), and aryl halides cleanly (unlike Wurtz coupling, works for unsymmetrical alkanes!).

example.label: Chemoselective conversion of benzoyl chloride to ketone (stops cleanly)

reagents.name: Haloform / Iodoform Reaction

reactivity.aldehyde: acetaldehyde (CH3CHO) ONLY -> CHI3 (yellow ppt) + HCOO-; other aldehydes -> no_reaction
reactivity.ketone: methyl ketones (R-CO-CH3) -> CHI3 (yellow ppt) + R-COO-; non-methyl ketones -> no_reaction
reactivity.alcohol: ethanol (CH3CH2OH) & 2°-methyl alcohols (R-CH(OH)-CH3) -> oxidized in situ -> CHI3 + R-COO-

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Oxidative C–C cleavage removes the terminal methyl carbon as CHI3 (yellow antiseptic-smelling precipitate), shortening the carbon chain by 1 carbon.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Base-catalyzed α-trihalogenation followed by acyl cleavage involves zero skeletal rearrangement.
reagents.conditions: I2 + aq. NaOH (or NaOI / NaOCl), warm
jeeTraps: Positive ONLY for CH3-C(=O)-R (R = H, alkyl, aryl) AND alcohols oxidizable to it: ethanol (CH3CH2OH) and R-CH(OH)-CH3 — methanol and propan-1-ol are NEGATIVE!
Acid derivatives with a CH3-CO- fragment (CH3COOH, CH3COOEt, CH3CONH2, CH3COCl) give NEGATIVE haloform test because leaving-group / resonance interaction prevents tri-iodination!
With Br2/NaOH on a 1° amide (RCONH2), the reaction is Hofmann bromamide degradation (-> RNH2 with 1 less carbon), NOT haloform!

example.label: Iodoform cleavage of a methyl ketone to benzoate + yellow CHI3

reagents.name: Cannizzaro Reaction (conc. NaOH)

reactivity.aldehyde: aldehydes with NO α-H (HCHO, PhCHO, Me3C-CHO) -> 1:1 alcohol + carboxylate; aldehydes WITH α-H -> Aldol instead!
reactivity.epoxide: nucleophilic ring opening at less hindered carbon

reagents.stereochemistryDetail: Rate-determining direct intermolecular hydride (H-) transfer between two aldehyde molecules; running in D2O incorporates ZERO deuterium on the reduced C–H bond.
reagents.rearrangementNote: Direct hydride transfer to a second carbonyl carbon involves zero carbocation rearrangement.
reagents.conditions: Conc. (50%) aq. NaOH or KOH, 25–100 °C
jeeTraps: Requires an aldehyde with ZERO α-hydrogens (HCHO, ArCHO, Me3C-CHO); aldehydes with α-H undergo ALDOL condensation instead (famous exception: isobutyraldehyde (CH3)2CHCHO gives Cannizzaro at high T!).
Crossed Cannizzaro with HCHO: formaldehyde is ALWAYS oxidized to HCOO- and the other aldehyde (e.g. PhCHO) is ALWAYS reduced to alcohol (PhCH2OH), because HCHO is more electrophilic!
Intramolecular Cannizzaro on phenylglyoxal (Ph-CO-CHO) gives mandelate (Ph-CH(OH)-COO-) because OH- attacks the more electrophilic -CHO and transfers H- to the ketone!

example.label: Disproportionation of benzaldehyde (no α-H) -> benzoate + benzyl alcohol
